absent: Full signature and contract of the instantiate helper beyond its dentry return and leading dentry parameter.
Bodies of the alternate address translation helpers for the second configuration.
Definitions, acquisition rules and failure modes of usage pinning, permanence testing, permanence marking, entry release and opener completion helpers.
Locking and lifetime rules for directory entry fields beyond opener list and sysctl linkage, including subtree structure and name storage.
Contracts of delegated file, inode and namespace operation handlers invoked through the proc wrappers.
Initialisation, locking and teardown of the global kcore list head and creation of its root entry.
Concrete enumeration values and access semantics for hide and subset modes beyond option emission.
User visible error taxonomy and mount behaviour beyond the handler signalling shown here.

findings.text: Exposes a generic write path for proc entries that requires a per entry handler with EACCES otherwise, accepts only non empty sizes below one page with EINVAL otherwise, copies user data with added termination, delegates to the handler, releases the copy, propagates duplication and handler failures, and normalizes a zero handler result to the requested length.
Provides a null tolerant helper that marks a given directory entry as permanent when the pointer is non null and does nothing otherwise.
Exposes registration for a single ram classification predicate with busy rejection on second registration, and appends descriptors carrying address size and type to a global kcore list.

Eviction discards page cache for the inode then clears it, detaches any tracked process identifier, and when a sysctl header is attached clears the pointer with single store semantics before invoking sysctl specific cleanup.
Sysctl inode cleanup removes the sibling linkage under protection and releases the header only when its reference count drops to zero.

Inode allocation obtains storage from a dedicated cache and initializes process, descriptor, link, entry, sysctl and namespace fields to neutral values with an empty sibling node, while release drops process and entry references before returning storage to the same cache, and a separate initializer prepares the embedded VFS inode.

Early initialization creates separate caches for proc inodes, opener records and directory entries with accounting and panic on failure, reclaim marking for inodes, and a usercopy region covering the inline name area, enforcing that the directory entry structure stays below its quantized container size.

Hide values map to distinct textual option tokens with a warning and fallback token for unexpected values, and mount options are emitted only when non default, covering group identifier, hide mode and pid only subset selection.

Seek, read, iterated read, write, mapping and unmapped area operations share a dispatch rule where permanent entries call through directly while other entries acquire a usage reference, invoke the delegated operation, then release, with acquisition failure reported as EINVAL for seek and EIO otherwise.

Poll and both ioctl variants follow the same permanent versus counted dispatch, returning a default poll mask or ENOTTY when no delegated handler exists, and counted acquisition failure yields the same defaults.

Open clears seek capability when the entry lacks seek support, calls the delegated open directly for permanent entries, otherwise pins the entry with ENOENT on failure, allocates an opener record with ENOMEM on failure only when a release handler exists, invokes open, and on success links the record for later release with proper unpin and cleanup. Release invokes the delegated handler directly for permanent entries, otherwise searches the opener list and completes the matching record.

Interrupt listing iterates by numeric position bounded above by the live interrupt count, advancing one step per iteration and terminating beyond the limit, with no cleanup action, bound into a sequence operations table and instantiated as a named entry during early init.

Kcore sizing starts from one note header and zero extent, extends over each listed segment end translated to file offset, counts one program header per segment, derives fixed header and note lengths plus page aligned data start, and publishes total length into the root entry size.
Ram classification delegates to the registered predicate when present and otherwise reports true.
Ram list construction allocates one descriptor spanning from the start of direct mapped memory over all low pages, tags it as ram, links it, and reports memory exhaustion on allocation failure.

One variant computes a page aligned memmap range for a ram segment, trims its end against overlapping existing memmap descriptors, appends a new memmap descriptor when non empty with allocation failure treated as benign, and reports success. A second variant reports success without action.

One precise helper derives per page mapping count with special type filtering and adds whole folio contribution for large folios, a second precise variant always traps, and an average helper returns direct count for small folios while for large folios it normalizes distributed counts over page count with rounding and a minimum of one.

The sysctl header count and sibling linkage must be mutated with the sysctl lock held, covering removal from the sibling set, decrement, and conditional deferred free decision as one critical section.
The opener list of a directory entry is protected by its unload lock for both insertion during successful open and lookup with completion during release.

Directory entry carries a usage counter and reference count, an opener list with its lock and optional unload completion, inode operations, alternative operation pointers for files versus directories, alternative sequence versus single show pointers, a write handler, opaque data, state and low inode numbers, link count, ownership, size, parent pointer, subtree root and node, external name pointer, mode, flags, name length and trailing inline name storage with randomized layout.

Proc inode wraps process identifier, numeric descriptor, a union for link resolution versus pid aware display versus LSM identifier, directory entry pointer, sysctl header and entry pointers, sibling hash node, namespace operations pointer and embedded VFS inode with randomized layout.
Opener record links into the entry list and stores the open file pointer, a closing flag and an optional completion pointer with randomized layout.

Maps traversal context holds a memory descriptor with optional per VMA lock state, while private state adds inode, task, VMA iterator, last position, locking context and optional NUMA policy with randomized layout.
Directory entry container size is quantized upward to fixed tiers with inline name capacity defined as the tier size minus the base structure size.

Non permanent entries use a usage count that is incremented on entry and decremented on exit, signalling unload completion when the count reaches a large negative bias value, with link put mapping directly to release and open failure paths guaranteeing balanced release.
Proc super operations bind allocation, release, direct drop, eviction, generic filesystem statistics and option display handlers.

Regular file operations bind seek read write poll ioctl mapping unmapped area open and release, iterated variants replace read with iterated read plus splice support, compat variants add compat ioctl, and link inode operations bind only link resolution.
Network sysctl and tty proc initializers are inert stubs reporting success or doing nothing in this configuration.

Callers must handle EACCES when a write handler is absent, EINVAL for empty or oversized writes, ENOENT on failed pin during open, ENOMEM for opener and kcore allocations, and EIO when pinning fails for data operations.

Absent delegated handlers must not be called and instead yield operation specific defaults covering EIO for data and mapping paths, default mask for poll, ENOTTY for ioctl paths, and architecture unmapped area fallback or original address for unmapped area resolution.
First process entry index is 256, numeric buffer length is 13, core flags value is zero, and unload bias is the most negative 32 bit value.

Kernel virtual address and kcore file offset interconvert by adding or subtracting the direct mapping base, device memory translation resolves through the direct map and its inverse is a no operation in this configuration.
Kcore maintains a root entry pointer, program header count, header and note lengths, data offset and an update flag initially requesting refresh.
Instantiate helper type names a factory returning a dentry and accepting at least a dentry argument.
Proc inode and opener caches reside in memory marked read only after early init.
